title: Superconductivity
text: Superconductivity is a phenomenon in certain materials where electrical resistance drops to exactly zero and magnetic flux fields are expelled below a characteristic critical temperature. It was first discovered in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes when he cooled mercury to 4.2 Kelvin. Materials that exhibit superconductivity are called superconductors. Conventional superconductors are explained by BCS theory, which describes electron pairs (Cooper pairs) forming bosons that can flow without resistance. High-temperature superconductors, discovered in the 1980s, operate at higher temperatures but are not yet fully understood theoretically. Superconductors have applications in MRI machines, particle accelerators, and maglev trains.
